ai.summary: CLI now renders ask_user prompts during the freebuff grace window by gating the session-ended banner on !askUserState. handleFreebuffGateError calls updater.markComplete() on session_expired or waiting_room_required to stop the streaming cursor and clear the flush interval. Fixes #518.

The session-ended message now appears correctly and stops the continuous loading indicator, so you can press Enter to rejoin. This restores control during the grace period and prevents the appearance of an unresponsive session.

ai.title: Tighten Fireworks prefill p90 degraded threshold to 500ms
ai.summary: Lowered `PREFILL_QUEUE_P90_DEGRADED_MS` from 1000 to 500 in `web/src/server/free-session/fireworks-health.ts`. The tighter threshold triggers 'degraded' status earlier, leveraging p90 as a leading indicator to halt session admission before median latency rises. Scope limited to server-side health checks for Fireworks backend.

eli5.text: Free sessions handled by Fireworks will now be marked as struggling when their slowest typical response takes longer than half a second, instead of a full second. The system uses this early warning to stop sending new sessions to that backend before most people notice things slowing down. If you watch response times right around the threshold, you'd see the 'degraded' flag appear sooner than before.

ai.title: SDK tests drop referralcode mock
ai.summary: SDK test mocks for user objects remove the `referral_code` field. This aligns test fixtures with the current schema after the field was dropped from the `user` table. Covers `run-cancellation`, `run-error-preserves-history`, `run-file-filter`, `run-handle-event`, and `run-mcp-tool-filter` test suites.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the development team updated their internal test setup to stop pretending a field called 'referral code' still exists on user profiles, because that field was already removed from the actual user database. This means nothing changes for you right now, but if you're a developer looking at the test code, you'll notice the fake user profiles no longer include a referral_code line. It's purely housekeeping to keep the tests matching the real data structure.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.644 release consolidates 17 fixes and CLI/web
ai.summary: Release version bumped from 1.0.643 to 1.0.644 in cli/release/package.json, packaging 17 user-visible updates shipped since the prior release. Notable changes include a CLI fix for grace-period hangs that rendered ask_user prompts during the freebuff grace window, removal of the /refer-friends command and referral UI from CLI and web surfaces, and agent-runtime now preserving message history across mid-run errors in loopAgentSteps. The release also tightened Fireworks health checks by switching from p50 to p90 prefill-queue latency with a new PREFILL_QUEUE_P90_DEGRADED_MS threshold of 500ms, switched the waiting room wait estimate to a fixed 24 seconds per spot ahead via WAIT_MS_PER_SPOT_AHEAD, and added team@codebuff.com bypass support plus a CLI model selector and /end-session command. Provider headers timeouts were raised from 10m to 30m across Canopywave, Fireworks, OpenAI, OpenRouter, and SiliconFlow to prevent premature connection drops for deep-thinking models.
ai.evidence: The diff in cli/release/package.json changes the version field from 1.0.643 to 1.0.644. The commit message confirms this as a release-bump consolidating 1.0.643 to 1.0.644, and the analysis notes list 17 user-visible updates included in this release spanning CLI, web, agent runtime, and provider health checks.

eli5.text: Freebuff 1.0.644 focuses on keeping the service running smoothly when AI demand spikes and fixing sticky spots in how you wait for your turn and pick up where you left off. The waiting room now gives you a friendlier, more accurate guess of how long you'll wait (roughly 24 seconds per spot ahead), and a special team email can skip the line entirely to keep automated tests from getting stuck. When you run out of time or hit a queue, the CLI now shows a clearer message and stops the spinning cursor so things don't freeze on screen. If a coding task gets interrupted mid-way, your conversation history is now preserved so you don't lose context when retrying. Under heavy load, the system automatically pauses new sessions faster to protect performance, and long-thinking AI models are no longer cut off after ten minutes, allowing deeper reasoning to finish. A few obsolete referral commands and banners were also cleaned out of the CLI for a simpler experience. Upgrading gives you a more stable, less glitchy experience especially during peak usage, with clearer signals when you're queued and fewer dropped conversations.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.40 release bundles Fireworks, CLI, and runtime
ai.summary: Version 0.0.40 packages the preceding days worth of Freebuff monorepo activity without introducing new code in this commit. User-visible changes span the agent runtime, CLI, waiting room, and provider health checks. The bump itself is a packaging artifact consolidating 1.0.643 to 1.0.644 CLI version, Fireworks p90 latency and KV block thresholds tightened, waiting room estimates switched to fixed 24-second-per-spot and bypass support added for team@codebuff.com, message history preserved across mid-run errors, and referral features removed from CLI and web surfaces.
ai.evidence: Diff in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` changes `"version": "0.0.39"` to `"version": "0.0.40"`. Analysis notes confirm this is a release-bump commit with +1/-1 stats.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.40 improves how you wait for and use AI coding help, making the experience smoother and more reliable. The waiting room now gives a simpler, more accurate wait-time estimate (24 seconds per person ahead), and developers on the free plan see fewer stalls when the system is busy. Chat history stays loaded while you browse past conversations, so you won't lose your place or get bumped back into line. If a long-running AI response gets interrupted, your progress is better preserved so you don’t lose work mid-session. The CLI now properly shows prompts during temporary grace periods instead of freezing, and account-suspension messages are clearer when they appear. Users on the free plan get a steadier experience overall, with quicker detection of slowdowns and cleaner handling of long-generation models.

ai.title: Block freebuff waiting room for disallowed countries
ai.summary: Added early country gate to freebuff session API. Rejects non-allowlist regions before queue admission via new `country_blocked` status. Covers CLI, Web, and shared types in `free-mode-country.ts` and `_handlers.ts`. Returns HTTP 403 to force older CLI backoff while new CLI parses body directly.

eli5.text: If you try to start a free-mode session (the waiting room before you get access to the service) from a country that isn't on the approved list, the system now immediately tells you 'Free mode isn\'t available in your region' and shows your detected country code, instead of letting you queue up and then rejecting you later. This is enforced at the session gate so the CLI, web, and shared types all see the same 'country_blocked' status and stop retrying; older CLI versions fall back to erroring out and backing off on their retry timer, while newer versions read the 403 response body to display the blocked message directly.

ai.title: Add bot investigation and ban scripts
ai.summary: New scripts `scripts/ban-freebuff-bots.ts`, `scripts/investigate-user.ts`, and `scripts/unban-user.ts` enable case-insensitive email lookups, DB schema joins, and bulk `banned` flag updates via Drizzle. `ban-freebuff-bots.ts` defaults to a dry run, requiring `--commit` to toggle `banned=true` and delete `free_session` rows for parsed candidate lists. `investigate-user.ts` aggregates message counts, costs, and repo usage by agent. `unban-user.ts` reverses bans for provided email arguments. `.gitignore` excludes `docs/bot-detection.md`.

eli5.text: The moderation team gained three new internal tools to manage bot accounts: a script to scan for and ban suspected FreeBuff bots (dry-run by default), one to investigate a user's activity, and another to unban users. These scripts interact directly with the user database to toggle bans, look up accounts by email, and report details like message counts and costs. The bot-detection guide is now excluded from version control. Effective immediately, these tools let staff block or restore access without touching application code.

ai.title: Add model selector and /end-session command
ai.summary: New `FreebuffModelSelector` component and `/end-session` command enable switching between model queues in the CLI waiting room. Selection persists to local settings and sends `x-freebuff-model` header on session POST; server 409 `model_locked` triggers UI confirmation prompt. Covers `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx`, `cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts`, and `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`. Migration `0044_violet_stingray.sql` adds queue depth tracking columns.

eli5.text: If you wait in the free session line in the CLI, you can now choose which model's queue you join. A new model selector appears in the waiting room, showing how many people are ahead for each model; tapping or pressing a number key (1-9) moves you to the back of that model's queue. You can also type /end-session to leave your current queue and return to the waiting room so you can pick another model. Your chosen model is remembered locally and sent to the server when joining; if the server says the model is locked (a conflict), a confirmation prompt asks you to confirm the switch.

ai.title: CLI status bar gains End session button and unified action rendering
ai.summary: StatusBar renders a dedicated End session button when idle with an active freebuff session, and StopButton is replaced by a shared StatusActionButton for hover-bold styling. A new END_SESSION_MESSAGE constant centralizes the waiting-room notice previously hardcoded in command-registry.ts. The end-session handler appends the system message and calls endAndRejoinFreebuffSession from chat.tsx, removing the redundant IS_FREEBUFF guard from the button render path. Scope limited to CLI chat UI components and constants.

eli5.text: When you're using a free trial session in the chatbot, the status bar at the bottom now shows a button that lets you end that session early and return to the waiting room. The old stop button was replaced with a more flexible button that can show different actions depending on the situation, and the message you see when you end the session is now stored in one place so it stays consistent across different parts of the app. If you're on a freebuff session and idle, you'll notice a clearly labeled End session button at the bottom that was not there before. This change is live today for freebuff session users.

ai.title: Improved Freebuff model selector
ai.summary: Refactored the CLI model selector layout using a row-based box structure for better visual separation. Moved the selector component above the status details in the waiting room screen. This change enhances readability and interaction flow within the CLI interface.

eli5.text: When you open the command-line app and land in the waiting area, the model picker now sits at the top, directly under the message telling you that you're in the waiting room. Below it, the estimated wait time and other status details are grouped together in their own box with consistent spacing. The picker itself uses the same row-based layout style as the rest of the screen, so the visual separation between choosing a model and reading your status is clearer and easier on the eyes while you wait.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.41 release bundles country gate, ban scripts, model
ai.summary: Freebuff is released as 0.0.41 in cli/release/package.json, packaging country-gating for the waiting room, new bot-investigation and ban scripts, a default token counter model switch to Claude Opus 4.6, an added CLI model selector and /end-session command, and an End session button in the status bar. The waiting room now rejects non-allowlist regions via the new country_blocked status and returns HTTP 403 to older CLI versions while new CLI parses the body directly. The model selector persists selections to local settings and sends the x-freebuff-model header on session POST, with server 409 model_locked triggering a UI confirmation prompt.
ai.evidence: Version bumped from 0.0.40 to 0.0.41 in freebuff/cli/release/package.json; the release updates list 8 items covering country gating, bot ban scripts, token counter defaults, model docs, CLI model selector and /end-session command, and status bar End session button.

eli5.text: This release adds a regional access check so Freebuff sessions start only in supported countries, introduces a model selector in the CLI waiting room, and adds a new /end-session command to gracefully leave a session. A new End Session button now appears in the CLI status bar when idle, and the waiting room shows a static wait-time message instead of a shimmering animation. Safety tooling for teams was expanded with scripts to investigate, ban, and unban users based on abuse, and the default token counter switched to Claude Opus 4.6 with documentation aligned to Claude Opus 4.7. Upgrading gives you smoother session control, clearer regional availability, and better protection against abusive usage.
